catalog_quote: Baucom (1974) lists twelve Wambo languages: Kwanyama, Kafima, Evale, Mbalanhu, Dombondola, Mbandja, Ndonga, Kwambi, Ngandjera, Kwaluudhi, Kolonkadhi and Eunda. He calls the first six languages Northern Wambo and the last six Southern Wambo languages. [...] Baucom (1974) states that all Wambo languages employ two “tone phonemes”. He makes two interesting observations [...] the Wambo languages differ from each other mostly in tone: “The Wambo peoples are very much aware of the lexical variation [...]” (Baucom 1974:53) He first states that there is much tonal variation from one Wambo variety to the next. [...] I have some tonal data of only four Wambo varieties out of twelve. In addition to Kwanyama, I have personally collected some data on Mbandja, and there is some published data on Ndonga and Mbalanhu.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for word stress is given for Ngandjera by any source found. Second-hand (Baucom 1972 via Halme 2004): every Wambo variety, Ngandjera included, is a two-tone language; nothing is said about stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Baucom (via Halme) notes 'much tonal variation from one Wambo variety to the next' and that the Wambo languages 'differ from each other mostly in tone'.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the Wambo (Oshiwambo) dialect cluster as a whole, of which Baucom's list explicitly includes Ngandjera as a Southern Wambo language; it concerns lexical tone (two tone phonemes) and says nothing about word stress or its position. Seen only as archive.org full-text-search snippets of a lending-restricted scan, not a full page.
new_statements.identity_note: Ngandyera = Ngandjera / Oshingandjera, a Southern Wambo (Oshiwambo, Bantu R24) dialect of the Ongandjera area (Omusati Region, Namibia) and adjacent Angola; Glottolog lists Angola only. Sister varieties with their own checks held by the project: Ndonga ndon1254, Kwambi kwam1251, Kwanyama kuan1247. The only quoted statement is about the whole Wambo cluster (Baucom 1972 via Halme 2004), which explicitly lists Ngandjera among its twelve members.
